issues.legal_issue: A purchaser seeking specific performance must establish continuous readiness and willingness to perform the contract from its execution through the decree.
Encashing refunded earnest money after the seller repudiates the agreement can establish the purchaser’s acceptance of that repudiation and cancellation of the agreement.
A suit for specific performance is not maintainable when the seller cancelled the agreement before the suit and the purchaser did not seek a declaration that the cancellation was invalid.
A beneficiary under a will concerning the disputed property has standing to appeal a decree affecting that property.
Suppressing the seller’s cancellation letter and accompanying refund from the plaint can disentitle a purchaser from discretionary relief of specific performance.
